subject: Isolated deployment economics & capacity recommendation
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna.li@medguard.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medguard.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: isolated deployment sizing for HIPAA workflow

Markus / Priyom,

Thanks for the call earlier — MedGuard is evaluating two paths for our LLM routing layer for PHI-handling flows: (A) Dedicated Reserved capacity hosted by Redwood (isolated tenant, shared infra) or (B) Private deployment inside our VPC with customer-managed nodes. We need a sizing recommendation that aligns to our Q4 pilot (10k monthly active users, 5–8 concurrent inference streams during peak) and a procurement ask for budget planning.

High-level constraints:
- Hard requirement: all PHI processing must remain in an isolated environment with SOC 2 traceability.
- Preferred latency: 100–200ms p95 for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Cost target: not to exceed $X/month for pilot (we'll share exact procurement band separately).

Can you send a concise comparison (required GPUs, expected p95 latencies, ops surface for audits, and procurement timeline) so we can feed this into procurement and our cloud infra team?

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks,
Anna Li
Head of Infrastructure 
MedGuard Health

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Anna Li <anna.li@medguard.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: isolated deployment sizing for HIPAA workflow

Anna — thanks for the clear constraints. We ran a quick pass internally and I wanted to share a short summary and flag two items we should confirm before giving hard numbers: (1) expected average request length and (2) percent of calls requiring context windows > 1k tokens (KV cache impact).

Preliminary summary (very high level):
- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated, isolated tenant): 2x A100-80GB equiv. for pilot (redundant pair), target p95 ~140ms under continuous batching, predictable monthly spend and Redwood-managed SOC2 evidence collection.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 3x A100-80GB equiv. (customer-managed autoscaling burst), target p95 ~120ms if colocated and tuned, but ops burden + audit ingestion falls on MedGuard.

I know that reads close; Priyom is looping in a detailed sizing workbook and assumptions. I'm attaching a capacity workbook draft and our SOC2 evidence summary to save procurement time.

Attachments: [capacity-model-v2.xlsx (sheet: assumptions, compute-mix, cost-projections)] [SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf]

Next steps: Priyom will follow with a breakdown by workload (chat vs. async batch), and Laura will outline contract lead times for a Dedicated commit versus Private licensing.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Anna Li <anna.li@medguard.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: isolated deployment sizing for HIPAA workflow

Anna / Markus / Laura,

Attached is a compact sizing workbook and the assumptions used for the numbers in Mark's note. Highlights beneath each sheet.

Key assumptions (sheet: assumptions):
- Pilot load: 10k MAU, 2.2 requests/user/day => ~22k requests/day.
- Peak concurrent inference streams: 8 sustained across a 15-minute window (spiky).
- Model: 13B dense / 1k token average per request for chat, 75% chat / 25% rerank/batch.
- Batching: Dedicated benefits from continuous batching; Private benefits if customer deploys identical batching layer.

Results (sheet: compute-mix):
- Dedicated hosted (isolated tenant):
  - Working set: piggyback on Redwood runtime optimizations.
  - Recommended pilot footprint: 2x GPU nodes (A100-80 or equivalent) configured as active/standby with autoscale to 3x during planned marketing spikes.
  - Observed p95 (simulated): 120–160ms for chat at 8 concurrent; throughput 600–900 req/min depending on batching window.
  - Operational overhead: low (Redwood handles kernel selection, KV caching, and SOC2 artifacting).

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - Recommended pilot footprint: 3x GPU nodes (same spec) with customer autoscaling + dedicated flow for audit log shipping.
  - Observed p95 (simulated), co-located network: 110–140ms — slightly better p95 if no multi-tenant serialization, but variance higher without our runtime telemetry.
  - Operational overhead: medium-high (customer responsible for KMS, network ACLs, evidence collection).

Cost/Procurement note (sheet: cost-projections):
- Dedicated: faster procurement (Redwood PO + commit), single bill, Redwood manages SOC2 deliverables; ideal if procurement wants OPEX and minimal infra work.
- Private: CapEx or marketplace listing depending on cloud partner; procurement lead time typically 6–10 weeks plus customer infra validation window.

Risk items to confirm before final estimate: token distribution tail, expected cache hit-rate, and whether you require private KMS/HSM for keying.

Attachment stub: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (sheets: assumptions, compute-mix, cost-projections).

--Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

If procurement needs a single-line justification for finance, use: "Redwood Dedicated reduces customer infra ops and consolidates audit evidence under Redwood's SOC2 program, shortening vendor validation windows."

I also attached a short SOC2 evidence summary we maintain for Dedicated customers — should speed legal review.

Recommendation (pilot):
- Start with Redwood Dedicated isolated tenant for the pilot. Rationale: predictable billing, faster provisioning (2–3 weeks), Redwood-managed SOC2 artifacting reduces procurement validation time. Recommended pilot footprint: 2x GPU nodes with autoscale to 3x for burst.

Procurement ask (suggested language):
"Purchase Redwood Dedicated pilot (isolated tenant) for Q4, 2x GPU reserved nodes with optional 3rd burst node. Redwood will provide SOC2 evidence and onboarding runbook. Pilot term: 3 months. Estimated monthly spend: refer to capacity-model-v2.xlsx cost projections."

If MedGuard requires the private deployment path for compliance reasons, we will prepare a tailored Private license addendum and SRE runbook; expect a longer lead time and higher customer-managed ops.

Next step: Anna, if you confirm you want to proceed with Dedicated we will issue a pilot SOW and slot provisioning for next week.
